Prescription of allopathic medicines
*101. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether doctors of Indian systems
of medicines cannot prescribe allopathic
medicines to patients; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Shortfall in realisation from
disinvestment
*102. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the shortfall in realisation from
disinvestment in the last three years;
(b) the estimates for the next two years;
and
(c) the measures being taken to expedite
the disinvestment programme?
Live telecast of Junior World Cup
Hockey match
*103. SHRI RAJNATH SINGH
’SURYA’: Will the Minister of
INFORMATION AND BROAD-
CASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that live telecast of
the final of Junior World Cup Hockey
match played in the month of October could
not be made;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether any request was received in
this regard from the Indian Hockey
Federation;
(d) whether there are any guidelines
regarding telecast of such important
matches; and
(e) if so, the reasons for their non-
compliance?
State funding of elections
*104. SHRI BALKAVI BAIRAGI:
Will the Minister of LAW, JUSTICE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Committee constituted
to consider the matter regarding State
funding of elections has since submitted its
report to Government; and
(b) if so, the details of the
recommendations made by the Committee?
AIDS project in H.P.
*105. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:

(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had sanctioned Rs. 395.58 lakh for
implementation of AIDS-II project in
Himachal Pradesh;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
Himachal Pradesh has implemented the said
project but Government have not released the
outstanding amount of Rs. 291.58 lakh to
them for which the State Government had
also written a letter on December 10, 1999;
and
(c) if so, whether Government have since
released the outstanding amount to the State?
Pendency of cases in Supreme Court
and High Courts
*106. SHRI  SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRI PRAKANTA WARISA:
Will the Minister of LAW, JUSTICE  AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the pendency of
large number of cases in the Supreme Court
and the High Courts in the country has shaken
the confidence of the people in the
administration of justice;
(b) the number of cases pending in various
High Courts (High Court-wise) and Supreme
Court as on 31st October, 2001, and the
number, out of them, which are pending for
more than a decade; and
(c) the steps taken or proposed to be taken
to bring down the pendency in Courts?
Housing problem of urban poor
*107. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN: Will
the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT
AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
considering to formulate comprehensive
action plan for solving housing problem
of the urban poor and those living in the
slums; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Setting up of district level Lok
Adalats
*108. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of LAW, JUSTICE  AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
set-up district level Lok Adalats headed
by retired Judges throughout the country
to settle expeditiously cases particularly
consumer related issues pertaining to
municipalities and service-oriented
services;
(b) if so, by when these Adalats are
likely to be functional; and
(c) the details in this regard?
Vacancies in Prasar Bharati Board
*109. SHRI KARTAR SINGH
DUGGAL: Will the Minister of
INFORMATION AND BROAD-
CASTING be pleased to state:
(a) the procedure for filling-up of the
vacancies and reconstitution of the Prasar
Bharati Board;
(b) the criteria for the selection of
Chairman and Members of the Board;
(c) whether there is a search panel to
do the scouting of talent for the selection
board; and
(d) why should it take more than a
year to fill in vacancies as has happened
of late?

WIN2\SESSION\3452RS
New package for development
of NER
749. SHRI PRAKANTA WARISA:
Will the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH-EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
announce any new package for the
development of North-Eastern Region;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the reaction of Government thereto?
Valuation of PSUs to be disinvested
750. SHRI AHMED PATEL: Will the
Minister of DISINVESTMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to disinvest some PSUs by the end of
March, 2002;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether proper valuation of such
PSUs has since been completed; and
(d) if not, on what basis the
disinvestment will take place in these
PSUs?
Disinvestment plan regarding ITDC
and HCI Hotels
751. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have adopted a flexible approach in its
disinvestment plans in the case of ITDC
and HCI Hotels;
(b) whether two of the better performing
hotels in Delhi and Bangalore are being
offered on lease while the remaining six are
to be sold outright;
(c) whether the funds that accrue from
the sale of five hotels will go to Air India to
enable it to clean up its balance sheet prior
to its disinvestment; and
(d) if so, the details of these plans?
Valuation of IPCL
752. SHRIMATI CHANDRA
KALA  PANDEY:
SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE:
Will the Minister of DISINVEST-
MENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned
164

165

"Fresh bids for IPCL sell off", which
appeared in the Telegraph, dated the
8th November, 2001;
(b) if so, Government’s reaction thereto;
(c) whether IPCL had engaged
M/s. Deloitte, Haskins & Sells to value assets
of IPCL, as reported;
(d) if so, the methodology of valuation
adopted; and
(e) whether the same is in line with
valuation method adopted, so far, for
Modern Foods, BALCO and others?
Valuation of IPCL’s Baroda unit
753. SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE:
SHRIMATI CHANDRA
KALA PANDEY:
Will the Minister of DISINVEST-
MENT be pleased to state:
(a) the status of purchase of IPCL’s
Baroda unit by IOC;
(b) whether the valuation by both the
companies are at wide variance;
(c) if so, the norms of valuation used by
IOC and IPCL;
(d) whether the same is in line with the
norms set by his Ministry;
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor; and
(f) the status of disinvestment of IPCL’s
other units?
Sale/lease of Ashoka and Samrat
Hotels in Delhi
754. SHRI SWARAJ KAUSHAL: Will
the Minister of DISINVESTMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Ashoka Hotel
was established by the first Prime Minister
of India for hosting foreign dignitaries and
their delegation members but Government
have decided to sell/lease the said hotel;
(b) whether Government have examined
the security aspects as the Ashoka and
Samrat Hotels are in close proximity of the
P.M. House; and
(c) whether Government have also
examined the alternative proposition of
hosting foreign dignitaries in other hotels
from the view point of their security and
hospitality on behalf of the country?
Disinvestment of Central Public Sector
Enterprises
755. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of DISINVESTMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Central Public Sector
Enterprises in operation, till date;
(b) the total investment made in all these
enterprises;
(c) how many of them are earning profits
and how many are incurring losses; and
(d) the disinvestment programme of
Government regarding these enterprises?
Disinvestment of NALCO
756. SHRI ANANTA SETHI: Will the
Minister of DISINVESTMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have a proposal
for the disinvestment of the National
Aluminium Company (NALCO);
(b) if so, the reasons for its disinvestment;
(c) the private companies which are
bidding in the disinvestment; and
(d) the details thereof?
